title: This, that, these, those, one
goal: Point to things near and far, one or many
intro: “This” and “these” are for things near you; “that” and “those” for things further away. This/that for one thing, these/those for more than one. To avoid repeating a noun, use “one” or “ones”: “I like the blue one.”

rules.rule: Use one/ones so you don’t repeat the noun.
examples: I don’t like this shirt. Show me that one.

mistakes.right: This type of person… / These types of people…
mistakes.why: Match the number: this type, these types.

ex.q: Who were ___ people at the gate?
The small cups are cheap, but the big ___ are better.
This kind of mistakes are common.
ex.fixed: These kinds of mistakes are common.

ex.q: Can you pass me that books?
ex.fixed: Can you pass me those books?

ex.q: I don't like the green, I want the red.
ex.fixed: I don't like the green, I want the red one.

ex.q: Look at ___ stars up there! (this / these / those)

ex.a: These are my old school friends.

ex.q: Correct this: “This clothes are very expensive.”

talk: Imagine you are in a shop. Ask about three things near you and far away. Use this, that, these, those, and “the blue one”.
